summary: This Standards Track document specifies BGP encodings and procedures for P2MP trees and Ingress Replication used in BGP/MPLS IP VPNs and EVPNs in a Segment Routing domain. It updates RFC 6514 and RFC 7988.

plainLanguage.summary: It explains how to send one message to many offices of a company over a shared network, using a branching tree.

questions: evpn ingress replication over segment routing
subtitle: How BGP advertises Segment Routing multicast trees and ingress replication for multicast and Ethernet VPNs.

tldr.problem: Multicast VPN and Ethernet VPN service providers need a way to carry customer multicast and broadcast traffic across a Segment Routing network, either on a controller-built tree or by sending separate copies.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines two new PMSI tunnel types for SR-MPLS and SRv6 P2MP trees, three new SRv6 endpoint behaviors, and BGP auto-discovery procedures that tie a tree's leaf set to the VPN routes. It also adds a Color Extended Community so ingress replication can have an SLA.
tldr.outcome: It is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 6514 and RFC 7988, and it asks IANA for two tunnel types and three SRv6 endpoint behaviors.

today: RFC 10018 is a Proposed Standard published in August 2026. It updates RFC 6514 and RFC 7988, and no later RFC obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Introduction and Scope
sections.content:
Multicast VPN (MVPN) lets a provider carry a customer's multicast traffic across its network inside Provider Tunnels (P-tunnels). RFC 6513 and RFC 6514 define the service. Those tunnels can be built in different ways. In a network that uses Segment Routing (SR), a P-tunnel can be an SR P2MP tree defined by an SR P2MP Policy (RFC 9960), or it can use SR P2MP Ingress Replication (IR).

This document covers both SR-MPLS and SRv6 data planes, for MVPN and for BGP MPLS-based EVPN (RFC 7432, updated by RFC 9572). It extends the BGP auto-discovery procedures of RFC 6514 for P-tunnels built with a P2MP tree instance (PTI), and extends RFC 7988 for IR with a Service Level Agreement (SLA).

Use of PIM for auto-discovery and support for customer BIDIR-PIM are out of scope. The reader is expected to know RFC 6513, RFC 6514 and RFC 7432.
sections.plainLanguage: A company wants to send the same news to all its offices through a delivery network. This document explains two delivery tricks for that, one with a branching road and one with many separate trips.

sections.title: The SR P2MP P-Tunnel
sections.content:
An ingress Provider Edge (PE) router steers customer traffic into a P-tunnel that is an SR-MPLS or SRv6 PTI. The PTI is instantiated by a candidate path (CP) of an SR P2MP Policy. The P-tunnel is announced in MVPN or EVPN auto-discovery (A-D) routes through the BGP PMSI Tunnel Attribute (PTA).

On the ingress PE, a conceptual MVPN/EVPN module talks to an SR P2MP Policy module. That module creates and updates the policy, the CP and the Leaf set, and signals them to a controller using protocols such as PCEP, BGP or NETCONF, which are outside the scope of this RFC. The controller computes the tree and stitches Replication segments (RFC 9524) at the Root, the intermediate replication nodes and the Leaf nodes.

The Tree-SID is the unique data plane identifier of the PTI. The Root encapsulates the payload in the Tree-SID, provider routers replicate it towards the Leaf nodes, and the Leaf nodes dispose of the Tree-SID and deliver the payload. A Leaf derives the MVPN or EVPN instance from the Tree-SID or from another context in the packet.

IR is different: the ingress PE delivers the payload to each egress PE itself, and neither the SR P2MP Policy module nor the controller takes part.
sections.plainLanguage: A planner builds a branching road from one office to all the others, and the road splits wherever needed. Each message follows the road and gets copied at the forks.

sections.title: Tunnel Attribute and SRv6 Behaviors for MVPN
sections.content:
A PTA for an SR P2MP P-tunnel uses one of two Tunnel Types: 0x0C for SR-MPLS P2MP Tree and 0x0D for SRv6 P2MP Tree. The Tunnel Identifier is the pair <Root, Tree-ID> from RFC 9960. Tree-ID is a 32-bit unsigned value that identifies the policy at the Root, and Root is an IPv4 or IPv6 address whose type is inferred from the PTA length. An implementation SHOULD advertise such a PTA only when the underlying data plane is supported.

When the tree is used by only one MVPN, the MPLS Label field is zero and the Tree-SID is enough to identify the instance. If a tree is shared by several MVPNs, the field must carry context. In SR-MPLS it MUST hold an upstream-assigned label or a label from a global context such as the Domain-wide Common Block (RFC 9573), and the ingress PE MUST impose it before the Tree-SID label. The cost is two MPLS labels to impose and dispose.

For SRv6, the document defines three endpoint behaviors, each like the matching RFC 8986 behavior except that the lookup is in a multicast table: End.DTMC4 (IPv4, AFI/SAFI 1/129), End.DTMC6 (IPv6, AFI/SAFI 2/129) and End.DTMC46 (either). A shared SRv6 tree uses an SRv6 Multicast Service SID carried in a BGP Prefix-SID attribute with the SRv6 L3 Service TLV, and it MUST be the last segment in the SRH. When the Transposition Scheme is used, the high-order 20 bits of the MPLS Label field carry the whole or part of the Function part of the SID. An egress PE MUST NOT install that SID in its FIB.
sections.plainLanguage: Each tree gets a name tag so everyone knows which road it is. If many companies share one road, each message also carries a small sticker saying which company it belongs to.

sections.title: Auto-Discovery Procedures
sections.content:
A PE creates a CP of an SR P2MP Policy when it originates an Intra-AS I-PMSI, an Inter-AS I-PMSI (for an intra-AS segment), an S-PMSI or a wildcard S-PMSI A-D route whose PTA has an SR P2MP tunnel type. It deletes the CP when it withdraws that route. When a PE originates an Inter-AS I-PMSI or S-PMSI route with this PTA, it MUST set the Leaf Information Required flag.

The ingress PE learns Leaf nodes by importing an Intra-AS I-PMSI or Leaf A-D route from an egress PE, and adds that egress PE to the policy's Leaf set. It removes the egress PE when the route is withdrawn. An egress PE joins as a Leaf or Bud node when it imports an I-PMSI or S-PMSI route with an SR P2MP PTA, and it MUST originate a Leaf A-D route if the flag is set. It withdraws itself, and that Leaf A-D route, when the ingress PE withdraws its route.

EVPN follows the same pattern with different routes: the IMET route plays the part of the Intra-AS I-PMSI route, and the S-PMSI and Leaf A-D routes of RFC 9572 are analogous to their MVPN counterparts. A PE creates the CP when it originates an IMET or S-PMSI route and MUST set the Leaf Information Required flag on an S-PMSI route with an SR P2MP PTA.
sections.plainLanguage: An office that wants the news raises its hand, and the sender adds it to the list of stops on the road. When the office leaves, it lowers its hand and is taken off the list.

sections.title: Ingress Replication with an SLA
sections.content:
With ingress replication, the ingress PE encapsulates the payload in SR-MPLS or SRv6 and sends one unicast copy to each egress PE. RFC 7988 already gives MVPN IR with best-effort unicast connectivity. This RFC adds an IR service with an SLA from the ingress PE to each egress PE, for both SR-MPLS and SRv6.

It does this by carrying the Color Extended Community (RFC 9012), with the Color-Only Type extension from RFC 9830, in BGP Updates for AFI/SAFI 1/129 and 2/129. The egress PE colors its Leaf or Intra-AS I-PMSI A-D route. The ingress PE then steers the payload into the matching SR-TE policy (RFC 9256) towards that PE.

In the SR-MPLS example, PE2 sends a Leaf A-D route with color C1 and IR label L10. PE1's SR-TE policy (C1, PE2) has segment list <L1, L2, L3>, so PE1 sends the label stack <L1, L2, L3, L10> with L10 at the bottom. For SRv6, the egress PE attaches a Prefix-SID attribute carrying an SRv6 Multicast Service SID, which MUST be routable within its AS, and the ingress PE puts it into the SRH.

The Color Extended Community is not used with an SR P2MP P-tunnel. Packets are replicated inside the tree, so the ingress PE sets the treatment for the whole tree through constraints and metric optimization on the CP.
sections.plainLanguage: Instead of one branching road, the sender mails a separate copy to every office. This document lets each office ask for a faster or safer route, tagged with a color.

sections.title: EVPN Specifics
sections.content:
For EVPN, the PTA is built as in the MVPN case, except for the MPLS Label and Flags fields. In SR-MPLS, a tree shared by several EVIs must carry an upstream-assigned or global-context label that identifies the EVI, imposed before the Tree-SID label. For SRv6, an EVI is always identified by an SRv6 SID in the SRH, even when the tree is not shared. The Endpoint behavior of the SID SHOULD be END.DT2M and the PE attaches the SRv6 L2 Service TLV.

EVPN needs split-horizon filtering with Ethernet Segment multihoming to prevent duplicate BUM traffic. In SR-MPLS, the existing P2MP LSP procedures from RFC 7432 are sufficient, with the ESI label at the bottom of the stack, then an EVI context label, then the Tree-SID label on top. For SRv6, the Arg.FE2 argument of End.DT2M identifies the Ethernet Segment of origin. The ingress PE merges it into the SID with a bitwise OR, and the egress PE uses it for filtering.

IR for EVPN follows the same colored-route approach as MVPN, with the egress PE coloring its IMET route. Inter-AS and Inter-Region segmentation procedures of RFC 9572 with SR P2MP P-tunnels are out of scope.
sections.plainLanguage: When two doors lead into the same house, you do not want the same news delivered twice. A small tag on each message tells the house which door it came from, so it is not repeated back out.

sections.title: IANA Code Points
sections.content: IANA has assigned two values in the PMSI Tunnel Types registry: 0x0C for SR-MPLS P2MP Tree and 0x0D for SRv6 P2MP Tree. It has also allocated three code points in the SRv6 Endpoint Behaviors registry: 76 (0x004C) for End.DTMC4, 77 (0x004D) for End.DTMC6 and 78 (0x004E) for End.DTMC46, all with IETF as change controller.
sections.plainLanguage: The new tree types and new behaviors each get their own official number, like giving every new game a number in the rule book.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC says the procedures introduce no additional security considerations beyond those in RFC 6513, RFC 6514, RFC 7432 and RFC 9572. For SR P2MP Policy and Replication segments, it points to RFC 9960 and RFC 9524.
sections.plainLanguage: Nothing new is added to worry about. The safety rules of the older documents still apply.
